title: Stability of School Academic Composition and Student Achievement Profiles: A Multilevel Latent Transition Analysis
abstract: School academic composition (SAC) describes the distribution of students across achievement levels within schools and provides an important perspective on academic differences between schools. However, few studies have followed the same student cohort to examine the temporal stability of SAC and transitions in student achievement profiles (SAPs) across initial school types. Using a two-wave longitudinal design, we analyzed individually matched examination records for 16,522 students from the same cohort across 48 high schools in a city in central China. These records linked students’ scores on the 2018 Academic Test for Junior High School Students (ATJHSS) and the 2021 National Unified Examination for Admissions to General Universities and Colleges (NUEAGUC). We first identified SAPs from standardized scores in Chinese, math, and foreign languages using a longitudinal mixture model. Multilevel latent profile analysis then identified SAC types from the within-school proportions of these profiles. Separate analyses estimated transitions between school types and SAP transitions conditional on initial school type and initial SAP. The models identified four SAPs and five SAC types with distinct combinations of these profiles. Modal class assignments indicated that 45 schools (93.75%) retained the same type across waves, while the remaining three transitioned to adjacent types. Estimated conditional retention probabilities for the predominant initial SAP within each initial school type ranged from 78.85% to 95.10%. The models also identified transitions to higher- and lower-score SAPs. These findings indicate that relative stability in SAC can coexist with changes in students’ relative academic standing. They provide descriptive evidence to inform SAC monitoring and assessments of student support needs.
